stillOwnedByThisShard.question: Is the fact Indiana never asks a genuine legal precondition that must be asked before a packet, or is the route not available to a self-help participant in Indiana?
stillOwnedByThisShard.answer: Neither, as stated — and the measurement says why. It is the second, but not because Indiana law closes the route: the product closes it.
finding: There is no missing fact. Driving the real evaluator with every rendered Indiana screen answered, in all five pathway-context options, returns missingQuestionIds: [] every time. Nothing a participant could answer changes any Indiana terminal, so a lifecycle classification correction in IN-indiana.json would move nothing.

The one fact Indiana never renders is record_documents, and UX-CONTENT-001 already records that record_documents has no eligibility, form, packet-selection or escalation consumer anywhere — its only named consumer in src is the drop-point nudge email. It is not a legal precondition.

Three of Indiana's four routes are held by name inside the shared evaluator. IN:non-conviction-arrest-or-criminal-charge-expungement and IN:juvenile-allegation-expungement are in CORRECTED_AWAITING_RECONFIRM_ROUTES and return needs_review with in.lawrence_reconfirmation_required; IN:conviction-expungement-with-records-marked-expunged is in HELD_GUIDANCE_ROUTES and returns guidance_only with in.lawrence_hold_guidance_only.

The fourth, IN:conviction-expungement-with-sealed-confidential-access, returns needs_more_info from compiled rule-03, whose own condition text states the cause: 'Because the supplied packet does not state every statutory eligibility tier for this route, the backend must confirm the applicable IC 35-38-9 section before packet release.' That rule's then-clause is frontendAction: return_to_exact_missing_questions while its when-clause has fieldsReferenced: [], so it sends the participant back to no question at all. The needs_more_info is unanswerable by construction, not by omission.

The root cause is visible in the profile itself. IN-indiana.json publishes two waiting-period rules and both are transcribed form boilerplate: wait-01 is '___ Said child is now at least nineteen years of age.' with no duration, and wait-02 is the CCA-XP juvenile checkbox pair. Indiana's real IC 35-38-9 tiers — one year for a non-conviction from the arrest date, five years for a misdemeanour, eight years plus three from sentence completion for a Level 6/Class D felony — exist only as hard-coded branches in specialRouteTiming inside src/lib/rcap-engine/evaluator.ts. The profile was converted from Indiana's court forms, not from the statute.
stillOwnedByThisShard.escalatedBecause: Both halves of the fix are outside this shard. The hold sets and the Indiana timing branches are in src/lib/rcap-engine/evaluator.ts, a prohibited path; and lifting rule-03 means re-converting IN-indiana.json from I.C. § 35-38-9 rather than from the Coalition for Court Access CCA-XP packet, which changes what the product claims Indiana offers. Indiana is also HELD_FOR_CORRECTION in data/expungement-ai/phase2/held-jurisdiction-dispositions.json with its pre-correction behaviour to be preserved exactly, and it is preserved exactly here.
stillOwnedByThisShard.askOfTheLegalOwner: Confirm whether Indiana's four routes are intended to be unavailable to a self-help participant in this release. If they are, the Indiana screening entry should say so plainly rather than ending in needs_more_info on a rule that names no question. If they are not, Indiana needs re-converting from the statute and the two evaluator hold sets need lifting, and neither is a state shard's change.

IN:conviction-expungement-with-records-m.rationale: Indiana publishes two waiting-period rules and neither is an adult-conviction rule. wait-01 has no duration at all and wait-02 is juvenile-form boilerplate. The real IC 35-38-9 conviction tiers are not in IN-indiana.json; they are hard-coded in the shared evaluator's specialRouteTiming, which this shard may not touch. The route is additionally in the evaluator's HELD_GUIDANCE_ROUTES set and returns guidance_only with in.lawrence_hold_guidance_only, so a binding would change nothing until the hold lifts and Indiana is re-converted from the statute.
IN:conviction-expungement-with-records-m.correctionNeeded: Re-convert IN-indiana.json from I.C. § 35-38-9 rather than from the Coalition for Court Access CCA-XP form packet, so the profile carries the statute's own conviction tiers; then lift IN:conviction-expungement-with-records-marked-expunged out of HELD_GUIDANCE_ROUTES in src/lib/rcap-engine/evaluator.ts.

IN:juvenile-allegation-expungement.rationale: wait-02 is the only juvenile-flavoured rule Indiana publishes, and it is a checkbox pair transcribed from the CCA-XP juvenile insert ('Select whichever event is later': the child is now at least nineteen, OR the child was discharged more than one year ago). It is a form instruction, not a compiled rule with an anchor, and wait-02 is already bound to two other Indiana routes. The route is in the evaluator's CORRECTED_AWAITING_RECONFIRM_ROUTES set, whose own comment says a qualifying case did not open payment because a required intake fact or anchor is missing.

MA:adult-conviction-sealing-under-m-g-l-.rationale: Massachusetts publishes the § 100A adult sealing wait as an explicit two-branch rule keyed on the offence level, and states it a second time in prose: 'Main adult sealing wait: 3 years misdemeanor, 7 years felony.' offense_level is a required, rendered screen in MA.

MA:adult-conviction-sealing-under-m-g-l-.caveat: MA also publishes wait-15 (sex offence: 15 years, or the registration-duty period, whichever is longer). It is keyed on offense_category / charge, which this flow does not put to the participant, so the sex-offence branch is named here but not proposed. Counsel decides whether the two-branch binding may ship without it.

MA:automatic-non-conviction-sealing-for-.rationale: No rule Massachusetts publishes states a waiting period for automatic § 100C sealing. The nearest, wait-06, says only that a subsequent not-guilty, dismissal, nolle prosequi or no bill 'does not interrupt the waiting period' — a tolling rule about some other route's clock, not this route's own wait. The pathway carries the general misdemeanor/felony sealing table, whose 3-and-7-year durations belong to § 100A. Reading either as this route's wait would be authoring.

No published rule attaches a duration to court-requested § 100C sealing, and the general table on the pathway is § 100A's. Substantial justice is a finding, not a waiting period.

A rule that says 'immediate unless X' cannot be bound as unconditionally immediate.

MN:arrest-identification-data-destructio.rationale: wait-01 is the only rule that names § 299C.11, and its recorded duration of 10 years is not a waiting period. Read the rule text: the ten years is a disqualifier lookback — the person must have 'no felony or gross misdemeanor conviction in the preceding 10 years'. Binding it as this route's wait would tell a participant arrested last week with a clean record to come back in ten years, which is the opposite of what § 299C.11 says. The route's actual wait, if any, is not stated anywhere in MN-minnesota.json.

evidence.anchor: successful completion of all sentence terms, if strict conditions are met
evidence.sourceText: Mississippi has a special first-offense DUI expungement rule. A person convicted of a first-offense DUI may petition the circuit court of the county of conviction at least 5 years after successful completion of all sentence terms, if strict conditions are met. The person must not have held a CDL or commercial learners permit at the time of the offense, must not have refused the blood/breath test, must have had a BAC below .16 if test results are available, must have no other DUI conviction or pending DUI, must justify expungement, and must not have previously had a DUI nonadjudication or expungement. The Mississippi Attorney General has also stated that a municipal court judge is not authorized to expunge a DUI conviction, although municipal or justice courts may handle expungement of nonadjudicated first-offense DUI charges in certain circumstances. ("https://attorneygenerallynnfitch.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/P.Booker_September-29-2020-Expungement-of-Drug-Related-DUIs.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com")

No published rule gives it a wait, and whether an expungement waiting rule should attach to a pardon referral at all is a legal question, not a lookup.

VA:automatic-sealing-no-filing.rationale: The § 19.2-392.7 automatic-sealing route carries three different waits in Virginia's own table and no participant answer separates them. Misdemeanour non-convictions and marijuana records seal with no wait; wait-01 and wait-05 give nine enumerated misdemeanour conviction types seven years; wait-02 and wait-06 give traffic infractions eleven. Which of the nine enumerated misdemeanours a record is, and whether a traffic matter is a criminal-traffic offence the rule excludes, are not facts this flow collects. Virginia's own profile also records that none of the sealing system is operational before 1 July 2026 (exclusion-21, exclusion-26) — the exact date the evaluator clock is pinned to.
